name: One-Concept Extensions of an Ample Forbidden Minor
statement: Let $S$ be an irredundantly embedded ample pc-minimal obstruction to dismantlable ampleness. Its ample one-concept extensions are in bijection with oriented punctured faces $(a,I)$ for which $a\notin S$, $I=I_S(a)$, every other vertex $a^U$ of that face lies in $S$, and $I\notin\operatorname{Sh}(S)$. Every such extension $E=S\cup\{a\}$ is either dismantlable ample or is itself an ample pc-minimal obstruction; the two outcomes partition the punctured-face atlas.
proof: The local one-concept test gives the bijection and makes $a$ a corner of $E$. Under any elementary restriction or contraction, irredundancy makes the image of $S$ a proper pc-minor and hence dismantlable ample. The image of $E$ is either that same family or an ample one-concept extension of it; in the latter case the surviving new concept is a corner and may be peeled first. Thus every proper pc-minor of $E$ is dismantlable ample. If $E$ peels it is in the positive part; otherwise it is an ample pc-minimal obstruction.
